sources.evidence: Jersey Dairy's current official site lists Jersey Dairy at La Route de la Trinité, Trinity, Jersey JE3 5JP and publishes its current milk, cream, butter, yogurt and ice-cream product ranges.

Jersey Dairy's current FAQ states that milk is pasteurised, that UHT milk uses sterilisation, that every batch of product processed by Jersey Dairy is tested on site, and that tours of the Jersey Dairy factory are offered to local school children.

The Government of Jersey records that all cow milk was processed at the central dairy run by the Jersey Milk Marketing Board and that the dairy moved in 2010 to purpose-built premises at Trinity, confirming the operator/site relationship.

The current official Isle of Man Creamery FAQ states that approximately 26 million litres of milk are processed each year at the Creamery and used to produce liquid milk, cheese, butter and cream; it also states that approximately 80 people currently work at the main Creamery building in Tromode.
The official history identifies the current Creamery home as the facility built in Tromode and describes today's operation as a factory processing milk.
The Isle of Man Government's current waste-site inspection register lists Isle of Man Creamery with a current inspection entry, independently supporting operational status.
